newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares seen coming off further.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares seen coming off further.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index lost 15.50 points to close at 10,026.91 on Thursday with market sentiment pointing to a continued downward trend for the coming month or so, brokers said.
"We saw some good volumes traded today but the downside in the index is still there," commented one broker.
The brokers say higher interest rates have been the downfall of the bourse by luring investors to the local money market.

They expect the share market to start recovering only after government unveils it's annual budget in July, and only if the budget promises reduced government spending, and hence lower inflation and interest rates.

The key index's loss on Thursday was precipitated by weaker deals in Alloys which shed 35 cents to 340, cement firm Porthold, down 25 cents to 1,850 while financial house udc, clothing retailers Edgars and electronics group Apex were all 20 cents easier at 260, 675 and 280 respectively.

But the secondary mining index inched 1,42 points higher to 967.95 with most counters trading at previous levels while copper producer Mhangura added five cents to 30 and coal miners Wankie lost 10 cents to 560.
